does_not_supersede: pilot_results.json / pilot_results.csv / router_comparison.json (left byte-identical; this file annotates them)

runtime.note: src/ is identical between 93cbd98 and HEAD, so the runtime code is pinned; the dirty flag is a provenance caveat recorded by the runs themselves.

defects.summary: The pilot manifest declared context_policy='task_scoped + stable_deterministic + identity', but every unit loaded experiments/configs/eval-benchmark.yaml, which contains no context: section. The resolved policy was therefore upstream_default and AtlasTaskPromptBuilder was never constructed.
evidence: experiments/evaluation/runner.py:350-400 (_context_prompt_builder returns None unless policy == task_scoped)
defects.consequence: All three runs used the upstream task prompt with legacy handoff. No ContextPlane block, selector, transform or renderer participated.

defects.summary: Multi-worker units gave each worker one sentence ('implement clean_rows', 'implement build_report on top of it') instead of the public requirement, the public interface contract and the public tests that the single-worker arm received in full.
evidence: experiments/evaluation/final4/runner_entry.py:57-67 (_worker_steps uses worker['objective'] as the whole prompt)
defects.consequence: R1 and R2 measured a decomposition that knew less than the task; R0 and N0 received the whole goal.

defects.summary: Both R1 workers ended with stop_reason=side_effect_unknown after a read-only git command returned a non-zero exit code, under tool_error_mode='legacy'. Neither worker wrote any file, so the exported patch was empty (sha256 of the empty string).
defects.consequence: The proximate cause of the R1 oracle failure is a worker-termination rule, not a context-handoff failure. This is the mechanism the phase-6 X0/X1 pair equalises, so that both arms differ only in context construction.

not_reusable_as: an arm of the corrected context comparison (context plane absent)

runs.failure_attribution: both workers stopped with side_effect_unknown on a failed read-only git command; empty patch; no worker output
reusable_as: evidence that a real multi-worker DAG executes two workers in one sandbox
a documented case of worker termination caused by a tool-error classification rather than by delegation itself
not_reusable_as: evidence that multi-worker delegation degrades quality
evidence about context handoff (no handoff ran)

reusable_as: evidence that the shipped router actually branches to DIRECT on a real proposal and that the collapsed plan is graded as a single-worker run
not_reusable_as: evidence that the router avoids harmful delegation (the proposal it judged was built from the unequal worker prompts)
a fair strategy comparison against R0/R1 (different task-level prompt content per worker)
evidence of a Context Plane benefit

budget_accounting.note: Consumed runs and cost stay counted against the Final-4 envelope. They are not refunded by reclassification.

reasons_for_reclassification: the declared Context Plane configuration was not loaded, so the treatment variable was absent
multi-worker arms received strictly less public task information than the single-worker arm
a worker-termination rule unrelated to context or delegation decided the R1 outcome
